question: India's longest river bridge, Dhola-Sadiya is being built on which of the following rivers?
solution:
The correct answer is __Brahmputra.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__​**

__
 
• **Dhola-Sadiya Bridge in Assam is India's longest river bridge.**
 
• Spanning 9.15 km, the bridge is built across the Lohit river, which is a tributary of the Brahmaputra.
 
• It will connect Assam and eastern Arunachal Pradesh. 
 
• The total length of the project, including the approach roads on each side, is 28.50 km.
 
• It is 3.55 km longer than the Bandra-Worli sea link in Mumbai. The sea link is the second-longest river bridge in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bogibeel bridge:

 
 
• Bogibeel bridge is a rail-cum-road bridge built over the Brahmaputra river.
 
• Bogibeel bridge is located in Assam.
